thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Pressured As Trade Jitters Offset Apple's Hotter-than-expected Earnings

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Stocks Pressured As Trade Jitters Offset Apple's Hotter-than-expected Earnings
text:
By Sue Chang, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
The Fed is set to release its policy update at 2 p.m. Eastern Time
U.S. stocks reversed early gains to trade mostly lower Wednesday as fresh worries over the U.S.-China trade friction overshadowed positive results from Apple and strong labor-market data.
What are benchmarks doing?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 83 points, or 0.3%, to 25,331. The S&P 500 shed 7 points, or 0.3%, to 2,809, but the Nasdaq Composite Index gained 9 points, or 0.1%, to 7,681.
What's driving markets?
Healthy earnings and a strong economic backdrop have buttressed the overall market even as a series of jitters have knocked stocks around. According to data from S&P Dow Jones Indices, 80% of the S&P 500 stocks that have reported second-quarter earnings so far have topped profit expectations, well above the historical average of 67%.
Robust iPhone sales helped Apple Inc. (AAPL) report its highest-ever revenue for the three months ending in June--typically a seasonally weak quarter for the tech giant. The results beat Wall Street expectations and Chief Executive Tim Cook provided an upbeat outlook for the coming quarter.
Shares rose 5.1%, with the stock climbing to a record. It has risen more than 18% thus far this year.
The news could help quell some fears about a deterioration in FAANGs, a quintet of stocks consisting of Facebook Inc. (FB), Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), Apple, Netflix Inc. (NFLX) and Google-parent Alphabet Inc.(GOOGL)(GOOGL). These stocks have been fueling the overall market's gains for years, including in 2018. However, both Facebook and Netflix have struggled of late, entering bear-market territory as their latest quarterly results suggest their era of sky-high growth rates may be drawing to a close (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-biggest-problem-for-facebook-and-netflix-is-they-are-running-out-of-humans-2018-07-30).
Despite Apple's positive news, market sentiment has been dampened by reports that President Donald Trump's administration has been considering increasing tariffs proposed on some Chinese imports, the latest escalation in tensions between the U.S. and its major trading partners.
The U.S. has already imposed 25% tariffs on $34 billion worth of Chinese imports and is on schedule to levy similar duties on an additional $16 billion of goods. The levies may be as high as 25% on an additional $200 billion of Chinese imports, up from the 10% tariffs originally proposed for those goods, The Wall Street Journal reported (https://www.wsj.com/articles/u-s-talks-with-china-over-trade-dispute-show-little-progress-1533066018?mod=hp_lead_pos1).
Concerns about an escalating trade clashes have intermittently created volatility on Wall Street and have reintroduced some anxieties Wednesday.
Those worries come ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy update at 2 p.m. Eastern Time, which isn't likely to offer any significant changes to policy, but may provide more clarity on the number of rate increases expected in the next five months. Markets have penciled in two further rate increases in 2018, beginning next month and in December.
The Fed statement will arrive ahead of the nonfarm-payroll report, an important reading of the labor market, on Friday.
Economic data in focus
Beyond the Fed policy update, the latest data on private-sector employment showed 219,000 jobs added in July (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-companies-create-219000-new-jobs-in-july-adp-says-2018-08-01), well above the 178,000 that had been expected.
Separately, the Markit manufacturing purchasing managers index came in at 55.3 in July. The Institute for Supply Management's July manufacturing index was 58.1%, below expectations for a reading of 59.5% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fast-growing-us-manufacturers-runn-into-more-roadblocks-in-july-ism-finds-2018-08-01).
What are market analysts saying?
"It's hard to separate trade negotiations from escalations in tensions. Both sides have taken shots and made threats, and we have to see how the dust settles. But clearly the risk hasn't been taken off the table, and the potential for a real escalation with China is much larger than it is with other trading partners," said Bruce McCain, chief investment strategist at Key Private Bank.
At the same time, he added, "Apple is reassuring people that the technology trade is not dead. This is a focal company and it should make investors feel better about the quarter overall, following some disappointments. The combination of the earnings picture and economic data is enough that investors won't lose their nerve and head for the hills, even if they're not overly enthusiastic."
"In my view the market is also struggling because of potentially higher interest rates. The ADP Private Sector Employment survey indicated strength, not weakness, hence the greater probability of two interest rate hikes. The 10-year Treasury is broaching the psychologically important level of 3.0%, the level which is/was associated with increased equity volatility," said Kent Engelke, chief economic strategist at Capitol Securities Management Inc. "Then there is the Fed meeting. No change in interest rates is expected but all are nervous about the Fed's view on inflationary expectations."
Which stocks are in focus
Humana Inc.(HUM) reported adjusted second-quarter earnings that beat expectations. It also raised its outlook (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/humana-beats-earnings-expectations-raises-outlook-2018-08-01). Shares rose 3.1%.
Restaurant Brands International Inc.(QSR)edged up (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/burger-king-parent-restaurant-brands-earnings-fall-short-of-estimates-2018-02-12) 0.2% after it reported adjusted second-quarter earnings that beat expectations.
Molson Coors Brewing Co. (TAP) reported adjusted second-quarter earnings that topped consensus analyst forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/molson-coors-stock-drops-after-earnings-report-as-us-revenue-falls-for-4th-straight-quarter-2018-08-01). The stock rallied 5%.
Pandora Media Inc.(P) spiked 16% a day after it reported second-quarter earnings and revenue that beat expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/pandora-expects-to-gain-more-listeners-through-partnerships-ceo-says-2018-07-31).
Ford Motor Co. (F) fell 1.9% after it reported a drop in its July sales (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fords-stock-slips-after-july-sales-data-as-declines-in-cars-and-suvs-offset-rise-in-trucks-2018-08-01).
The Wall Street Journal reported that activist investor Third Point LLC has built a stake of more than $300 million (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/daniel-loebs-third-point-has-built-300-million-stake-in-campbell-soup-2018-07-31) in Campbell Soup Co.(CPB), citing a person familiar with the matter. The stock rose 1.8%.
Tesla Inc. (TSLA) will likely be in focus throughout the session. The electric-car company, shares of which have been extremely volatile throughout 2018, is scheduled to report its quarterly results after the market closes (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tesla-earnings-investors-should-gear-up-for-more-drama-2018-07-19). Shares are off 0.9%; it has lost nearly 13% over the past month.
What are other markets doing?
European stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-pull-back-on-risk-of-us-hike-in-chinese-tariffs-2018-08-01) were down across the region, while Asian markets (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-mostly-up-as-apple-suppliers-get-a-boost-2018-07-31) were mixed with China weaker but Korea and Japan higher.
The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield is trading at 2.99% after touching 3% for the first time since June (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/treasury-yields-rise-japanese-bonds-suffer-biggest-selloff-in-2-years-2018-08-01).
U.S. oil (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-slide-on-surprise-rise-in-us-stockpiles-2018-08-01) futures were down 1.5% to $67.73 and gold futures (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gold-slips-as-fed-policy-update-comes-into-focus-2018-08-01) shed 0.5%. The ICE U.S. Dollar Index (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-edges-higher-with-the-fed-and-trade-worries-back-in-focus-2018-08-01) edged up 0.2%.
